newsitem.title: USA: U.S. primary aluminum shipments dip in Jan to Oct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. primary aluminum shipments dip in Jan to Oct.

text.p: U.S. primary aluminum shipments in the first ten months of the year fell 2.7 percent to 17.464 billion pounds or 7,921,546 tonnes, the Aluminum Association reported.

Preliminary figures for October indicated that industry shipments, including exports, totaled 1.821 billion pounds, a rise of 7.7 percent from October 1995, and up 8 percent from a revised September total of 1.686 billion.
U.S. exports of aluminum ingot and mill products were 266 million pounds in October, up 13 percent over the same month last year.
Imports in October rose 21.7 percent to 502 million pounds over the same month in 1995.
Estimated industry net new orders of aluminum mill products totaled 1.152 billion pounds in November, down 9.4 percent from November last year.

New orders for domestic can stock totaling 262 million pounds in November, were down 21.4 percent from November 1995. Orders for other sheet and plate, including exports, were down 8.6 percent to 462 million over the same period.

In the first eleven months of the year, industry orders totaled 13.673 billion pounds, up 1.6 percent on the same period last year. New orders of domestic can stock have declined 9.9 percent while orders for other sheet and plate rose 9.4 percent.
Producer inventories in October totaled 4.041 billion pounds, down 139 million from September.
Scrap consumption rose 15.8 percent to 741 million pounds in October compared to the same month last year.
